name: DaBaby
notes: The research names one parameter explicitly and calls it distinctive: "semitone-neighbour ostinato over a static tonic" — motifs built on chromatic half-step oscillation rather than chord progressions, the "Suge" line moving between the upper A and Bb. That is authored three ways at once: `halfStepDissonance` 0.32 (the highest in this batch by a wide margin), a step-dominant interval set at 0.8 because a semitone neighbour IS a step, and `bassline.passingTones` led by `m2` — the only entry here that uses it. Everything else is jetsonmade's deliberate un-layering: one synth voice carries the hook (`square_lead`, `countermelody.densityRatio` at the 0.3 floor), 2-bar loops, 2–4 pitch sets, and `endVariation: false` because the research says the hook repeats verbatim with no melodic variation. The open-hat accents that mark bar ends are the batch's highest `openHat.prob`, pinned to `4&`. Rolls are restrained per the research, so this file carries the lowest `snareRoll` jitter and the highest `gapProb` here. ⚠ `high` — producer interviews describe the construction and palette explicitly, which is why this is the only `high` in this batch. ⚠ `chords.impliedByRiff` is set: the research says the motifs are not chord progressions. The i–VII family is INFERRED and carries the low weight — the research names only a static tonic — and is the first thing to delete if this ever sounds more harmonic than the records. ⚠ The "almost double-time" snare feel is authored as `fullTimeVariantProb` 0.25 over the half-time placement, not as a tempo change. ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts.
